messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete web app for creating, fixing, and updating Minecraft Bedrock/MCPE add-ons, with live web research and support for remote GGUF model servers.

## Requirements
- User requested an implementation, not a plan; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- GGUF models run on a separate server to avoid overloading Android or other devices.
- User also requested a playable game, but the main app task is an add-on studio.

## Decisions
- Built a responsive single-page “Blocksmith” studio with browser-based demo generation and an optional OpenAI-compatible server connection.
- Changed the default pack type to “Behavior + resource” so generated custom entities can include rendering resources.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `app.js` for the add-on studio UI and interactions.
- Added demo pack generation, file previews, `.mcaddon` ZIP download, project library, validator, documentation links, web research/search UI, and server settings for remote model endpoints.
- Verified `app.js` syntax with `node --check app.js`.
- Opened the app at `http://localhost:3002` and verified demo generation in Playwright.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/blocksmith.jpg`.

### Active
- Improve generated custom entity packs: add a matching resource-pack client entity definition, ensure behavior/resource dependency is correct, and improve tame/friendly behavior.
- Recheck generated output, including validity and ZIP download behavior.

### Blocked
- Browser emitted a 404 for `/favicon.ico`; currently non-blocking.
- Live DuckDuckGo preview fetch may be blocked by browser CORS; UI falls back to direct search links and official docs.

## Next Move
1. Update `makePack()` in `app.js` to add a client entity resource definition for custom entities and correctly link behavior/resource pack manifests.
2. Consider improving the default entity behavior to match tame/guard prompts, and sanitize model-generated file paths.
3. Re-run syntax checks and browser-test generation/download after changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main studio interface and views.
- `style.css`: Responsive dark studio styling.
- `app.js`: Generation logic, model connection, search, validation, ZIP download, and project library.
- `screenshots/blocksmith.jpg`: Latest inspected desktop screenshot.

## Important Context
- A Python HTTP server was started on port `3002`.
- The `.mcaddon` download is built client-side using a custom ZIP implementation.
- Demo generation currently creates entity starter JSON and pack manifests; entity client-rendering assets and taming behavior still need refinement.

## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a web app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons using browser demo generation or a remote model server.
- Add a separate role-playing mode that can use a large-context model on a server and deliver replies to a tablet.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server, not on the tablet.
- Role-playing should be a separate mode; the user asked for “a 2m context or more” and “safety features reduced or none (if possible).”
- The app should support live web research and add-on creation, fixing, and updates.

## Decisions
- The add-on studio uses browser-based demo generation or an optional OpenAI-compatible server.
- Entity packs include a resource-pack client definition and behavior-to-resource manifest dependency; tame/follow behavior is generated for pet/companion prompts.

- Determine how to communicate/configure a 2-million-token context target while clarifying that actual context capacity depends on the selected model and server.

2. Connect chat requests to the configured OpenAI-compatible server and retain conversation history appropriately.

- `index.html`: Studio views, navigation, and server settings UI.
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, server requests, and app interactions.
- `style.css`: Responsive studio styling.

- The local app at `http://localhost:3002` responded with HTTP 200 after the latest changes.
- Repository files were untracked at the last `git status --short`; changes are not committed.
- No role-play code has been added yet.

## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons.
- Add a separate, tablet-friendly role-play mode that sends chat to a remote model server.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; the tablet receives replies.
- Target 2M-token context or more, while recognizing that actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Role-play remains separate from add-on creation; safety policies enforced by the model or server are not overridden.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends the conversation history.
- The 2M context target is informational, not a setting that can enlarge model or server capacity.
- Conversation history and the character/scene prompt are saved in browser storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, and `.mcaddon` generation.
- Added a separate role-play view with character/scene prompt, persistent chat history, send/reply flow, clear-chat control, and mobile mode switch.
- Added messaging clarifying context limits and that the app does not override server/model safety policies.
- `node --check app.js` and static HTML/ID checks passed.

### Active
- Verify role-play requests and tablet layout against a reachable OpenAI-compatible server.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test the role-play flow with a configured server, including server errors and long-history limits.
2. Check the role-play view on a tablet-sized browser and refine if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Navigation, role-play view, and connection settings.
- `app.js`: Server requests, add-on generation, and role-play history/chat.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and role-play styling.

## Important Context
- Add-on generation and `.mcaddon` packaging were previously verified, including syntax, JSON/dependencies, and ZIP integrity.
- The 2M context label does not control request limits; long chat requests may exceed server/model capacity or browser storage.
- Changes remain uncommitted; repository files are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons.
- Provide a separate, tablet-friendly role-play mode that sends chat to a remote model server.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; the tablet receives replies.
- Target a 2M-token context or more, while noting actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Keep role-play separate from add-on creation; do not override model or server safety policies.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M context target is informational, not a setting that can enlarge model or server capacity.
- Conversation history and character/scene prompt are saved in browser storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, and `.mcaddon` generation.
- Added a separate role-play view with persistent chat history, character/scene prompt, send/reply flow, clear-chat control, and mobile mode switch.
- Added context-limit and safety-policy messaging.
- `node --check app.js`, static HTML/ID checks, and `git diff --check` passed; Chromium headless loaded the app.

### Active
- Verify role-play requests and error handling against a reachable OpenAI-compatible server.
- Verify and refine the role-play view at tablet-sized browser dimensions; the screenshot attempt remained on the add-on creation view.

### Blocked
- Live server testing is pending a configured, reachable OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## Next Move
1. Test role-play success, server errors, and long-history behavior with a configured endpoint.
2. Open the role-play view at tablet dimensions and refine layout if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Navigation, role-play view, and connection settings.
- `app.js`: Server requests, role-play chat/history, and add-on generation.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and role-play styling.

## Important Context
- Add-on generation and `.mcaddon` packaging were previously verified, including syntax, JSON/dependencies, and ZIP integrity.
- Long chats may exceed server/model capacity or browser storage; the 2M context label does not control request limits.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files are untracked.

## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons.
- Provide a separate, tablet-friendly role-play mode that sends chat to a remote model server.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; the tablet receives replies.
- Target 2M-token context or more, while noting actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Keep role-play separate from add-on creation; do not override model or server safety policies.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M context target is informational, not a setting that can enlarge model or server capacity.
- Conversation history and character/scene prompt are saved in browser storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, and `.mcaddon` generation.
- Added separate role-play view with persistent chat history, character/scene prompt, send/reply flow, clear-chat control, and mobile mode switch.
- Added context-limit and safety-policy messaging.
- Tested role-play success and simulated HTTP 503 handling against a local mock OpenAI-compatible server; confirmed history is sent across turns, failed input is restored, and failed user turn is removed from saved history.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest CSS edit.

### Active
- Fix tablet layout: at 820×1180, the role-play chat remains too narrow; the added `@media(max-width:920px)` rule is overridden by later default `.roleplay-layout` styles.
- Test long-history behavior and recheck layout after correcting CSS rule order.

### Blocked
- Live testing against the intended model server is pending a configured, reachable endpoint; only the local mock server was available.

## Next Move
1. Move or adjust the tablet role-play CSS override so it takes precedence over default layout styles, then inspect at 820×1180.
2. Exercise long conversation history against the mock server and rerun syntax/diff checks.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode using a remote model server.
- Add support for uploading `.mcaddon` files to inspect and repair them, and/or improve generation of complex add-ons with many features.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; the tablet receives replies through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Target 2M-token context or more is informational only; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Keep role-play separate from add-on creation, and do not override model or server safety policies.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage.
- The new add-on request specifically asks to accept uploaded `.mcaddon` files to unzip, analyze, and fix them; complex feature-rich generation is also requested as a possible direction.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- No implementation approach or priority has yet been decided for archive inspection/repair versus complex add-on generation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, and `.mcaddon` generation.
- Added a separate role-play view with persistent chat history, character/scene prompt, send/reply flow, clear-chat control, mobile mode switch, and context/safety messaging.
- Tested successful role-play turns and simulated HTTP 503 handling against a local mock server; verified history is sent across turns, failed input is restored, and the failed user turn is removed from saved history.
- Added a tablet CSS override at the end of `style.css`; `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed afterward.

### Active
- Fix tablet role-play layout: the latest 820×1180 screenshot still shows a narrow chat area; harness reported `.roleplay-layout` width 495 and document scroll width 790.
- Implement uploaded `.mcaddon` archive extraction, analysis, and repair support, or determine the intended scope alongside feature-rich generation.
- Test long conversation history against the mock server and recheck responsive layout.

### Blocked
- Live testing against the intended model server is pending a configured, reachable endpoint.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the validator flow and implement safe in-browser `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archive inspection with useful diagnostics and repair actions.
2. Clarify or scope complex feature-rich generation relative to upload-and-repair support.
3. Diagnose the tablet width/overflow issue, test long chat history, and rerun syntax/diff checks.
4. Test with the configured model endpoint when available.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Studio, validator upload UI, and role-play view.
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, validator, model requests, role-play history and persistence.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and the latest tablet override.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness for role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- Validator UI accepts `.mcaddon` and `.mcpack` files, but current archive handling only reports that inspection is unavailable; JSON files can be checked directly.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the latest `git status`.
- The local mock server uses `127.0.0.1:8766`; HTTP 503 is simulated with `trigger-error`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating and validating Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode using a remote model server.
- Add support for uploading `.mcaddon` files to inspect and repair them, or improve generation of add-ons with many features.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; the tablet receives replies through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Target 2M-token context is informational only; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Keep role-play separate from add-on creation, and do not override model or server safety policies.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage.
- The user asked: “Oh! Can it like accept uploaded .mcaddons too? (For it to unzip, analyze and fix the addon) [or for it to make a very complex addon with lots lots of features.]”

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- No implementation approach or priority has been decided for archive inspection/repair versus complex add-on generation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, and `.mcaddon` generation.
- Added a separate role-play view with persistent chat history, character/scene prompt, send/reply flow, clear-chat control, mobile mode switch, and context/safety messaging.
- Tested successful role-play turns and simulated HTTP 503 handling against a local mock server; verified history is sent across turns, failed input is restored, and the failed user turn is removed from saved history.
- Updated the validator’s `index.html` description to say archives can be inspected and repaired; implementation has not yet been added.

### Active
- Implement safe in-browser `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archive inspection and repair; current archive handling still says inspection is unavailable.
- Diagnose the tablet role-play layout: the latest 820×1180 screenshot showed a narrow chat area (`.roleplay-layout` width 495; document scroll width 790).
- Test long conversation history against the mock server and recheck responsive layout.

### Blocked
- Live testing against the intended model server is pending a configured, reachable endpoint.

## Next Move
1. Implement safe archive extraction, validation, repair actions, and download while preserving binary assets.
2. Clarify or scope complex feature-rich generation relative to upload-and-repair support.
3. Diagnose tablet width/overflow, test long chat history, and rerun syntax/diff checks.
4. Test with the configured model endpoint when available.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Studio, validator upload UI, and role-play view; validator copy was updated ahead of implementation.
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, validator, model requests, role-play history and persistence; archive handling remains unavailable.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and tablet role-play styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness for role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- The attempted `app.js` edit to implement archive inspection failed because the exact source text did not match; no archive implementation was added.
- The validator accepts `.mcaddon` and `.mcpack` uploads, but currently only checks JSON files directly and reports compressed-archive inspection as unavailable.
- Project files are uncommitted and were untracked in the latest `git status`.

## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating, validating, and repairing Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode.
- Add uploaded-video analysis to help infer animation movements and targets, and use that information when generating add-ons.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Accept `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` uploads for in-browser inspection and safe repair while preserving binary assets.
- Analyze uploaded videos to understand animation movement and targets.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M-token context target is informational; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- No archive-repair implementation approach or complex-generation scope has been decided.
- Video UI notes that analysis requires a vision-capable configured server and uses sampled frames; the analysis flow is not implemented yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator UI, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, and separate persistent role-play view.
- Tested role-play turns and simulated HTTP 503 handling against a local mock server.
- Updated validator copy to promise archive inspection/repair.
- Added video-reference controls to the creation UI in `index.html` (`#videoInput`, `#analyzeVideo`, `#videoAnalysis`).

### Active
- Implement safe in-browser `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` extraction, validation, repair, and download; current handling still says archive inspection is unavailable.
- Implement video frame sampling and analysis through a vision-capable server, then make the analysis usable in add-on generation.
- Diagnose tablet role-play width/overflow and test long conversation history.

### Blocked
- Live testing against the intended model server requires a configured, reachable endpoint; video analysis also requires a vision-capable model.

## Next Move
1. Implement safe archive extraction and repair while preserving binary files; the previous `app.js` edit failed because its exact source text did not match.
2. Implement the video upload/analyze flow and connect its findings to generation; report clearly when the configured model cannot process images.
3. Fix and retest tablet role-play layout and long-history behavior.
4. Run syntax/diff checks and test against a configured model endpoint when available.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App views, validator UI, and newly added video-reference controls.
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, archive validator (currently unavailable), and role-play persistence/requests.
- `style.css`: Responsive and role-play layout styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness for role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and were untracked in the latest `git status`.
- The validator accepts `.mcaddon` and `.mcpack` uploads but does not yet inspect compressed archives.
- The video UI was added, but no video sampling or vision request code has been added.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating, validating, and repairing Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode.
- Analyze uploaded videos for animation movement and targets, then use those findings in add-on generation.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Inspect and safely repair `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archives in-browser while preserving binary assets.
- Analyze uploaded videos to understand animation movement and targets.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M-token context target is informational; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Archive inspection/repair uses JSZip via CDN, with file-count, size, expanded-size, and path-safety limits.
- Video analysis samples up to five frames and requires an image-capable configured server; findings are passed into server-based generation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator UI, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, and persistent role-play view.
- Tested role-play turns and simulated HTTP 503 handling against a local mock server.
- Added video-reference controls to `index.html`.
- Added JSZip CDN loading and implemented initial archive inspection/manifest-repair flow in `app.js`.
- Added video sampling, vision endpoint requests, and passing analysis findings into server generation.

### Active
- Validate the new archive and video code for syntax and behavior; archive repair currently handles valid manifest JSON fields, while malformed JSON is left unchanged.
- Fix and retest tablet role-play layout and long-history behavior.
- Run syntax/diff checks and test against a configured model endpoint when available.

### Blocked
- Live testing requires a configured, reachable model server; video analysis additionally requires a vision-capable model.

## Next Move
1. Run syntax checks and inspect the recent `app.js` edits for implementation errors.
2. Test archive extraction, validation, safe-path handling, manifest repair, and binary preservation with sample `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` files.
3. Test video frame sampling and vision requests; improve error feedback for endpoints that reject image inputs.
4. Fix and retest tablet role-play layout and long-history behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App views, validator UI, video controls, and JSZip CDN script.
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, archive inspection/repair, video analysis, and role-play persistence/requests.
- `style.css`: Responsive and role-play layout styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server used for prior role-play tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness used for prior role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and were untracked in the latest `git status`.
- The new archive/video implementations have not yet been syntax-checked or browser-tested.
- Archive inspection depends on loading JSZip from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating, validating, and repairing Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode.
- Analyze uploaded videos for animation movement and targets, then use those findings in add-on generation.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Inspect and safely repair `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archives in-browser while preserving binary assets.
- Analyze uploaded videos to understand animation movement and targets.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M-token context target is informational; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Archive inspection/repair uses JSZip via CDN, with file-count, size, expanded-size, and path-safety limits.
- Video analysis samples up to five frames and requires an image-capable configured server; findings are passed into server-based generation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator UI, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, and persistent role-play view.
- Added archive inspection/manifest-repair flow and video frame sampling/vision requests.
- Ran `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` successfully.
- Fixed archive path NUL checking, the `world_template` module type, a duplicate validator function, and handling of non-object manifest JSON.

### Active
- Validate archive extraction, safe-path handling, manifest repair, and binary preservation with sample archives.
- Test video frame sampling and vision requests; improve feedback for endpoints that reject image inputs.
- Fix and retest tablet role-play layout and long-history behavior.
- Run browser tests and test against a configured model endpoint when available.

### Blocked
- Live model testing requires a configured, reachable model server; video analysis additionally requires a vision-capable model.
- A local HTTP server attempt on port 3002 failed because the port was already in use.

## Next Move
1. Run browser checks against the existing local server and inspect tablet role-play layout.
2. Test archive extraction, validation, safe-path handling, manifest repair, and binary preservation with sample `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` files.
3. Test video sampling and vision requests, including endpoint error feedback.
4. Retest role-play behavior with long history and a configured model endpoint.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Archive validation/repair, video analysis, generation, and role-play logic.
- `index.html`: App views, validator UI, video controls, and JSZip CDN script.
- `style.css`: Responsive and role-play layout styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server used for prior role-play tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness used for prior role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- Project files remain uncommitted and appear as untracked files in `git status`.
- Archive/video implementations have not yet been browser-tested; malformed JSON remains unchanged during archive repair.
- Archive inspection depends on loading JSZip from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build Blocksmith, a browser app for creating, validating, and repairing Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with a separate tablet-friendly role-play mode.
- Analyze uploaded videos for animation movement and targets, then use those findings in add-on generation.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Save role-play history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Inspect and safely repair `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archives in-browser while preserving binary assets.
- Analyze uploaded videos to understand animation movement and targets.

## Decisions
- Role-play uses the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint and sends conversation history.
- The 2M-token context target is informational; actual capacity depends on the selected model and server.
- Archive inspection/repair uses JSZip via CDN, with file-count, size, expanded-size, and path-safety limits.
- Video analysis samples up to five frames and requires an image-capable configured server; findings are passed into server-based generation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator UI, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, and persistent role-play view.
- Added archive inspection/manifest-repair flow and video frame sampling/vision requests.
- Browser-loaded the app from the existing local server on port 3002; confirmed JSZip loads.
- Found and fixed an archive extension-matching regex in `app.js`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed after the regex and unsafe-path-removal changes.

### Active
- Retest unsafe archive path removal after fixing JSZip’s normalized-name behavior; verify malformed JSON remains unchanged and binary assets are preserved in the repaired output.
- Test video frame sampling and vision endpoint error feedback.
- Inspect tablet role-play layout and long-history behavior.
- Run role-play and generation tests against a configured model endpoint when available.

### Blocked
- Live model testing requires a configured, reachable model server; video analysis additionally requires a vision-capable model.

## Next Move
1. Reload the browser app, inspect `/tmp/opencode/sample2.mcaddon`, download the repaired copy, and verify unsafe entries are absent, malformed JSON is unchanged, and binary data is preserved.
2. Test video sampling and vision requests, including endpoint error feedback.
3. Check role-play layout at tablet width and long-history behavior; test against the configured model endpoint if available.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Archive validation/repair, video analysis, generation, and role-play logic.
- `index.html`: App views, validator UI, video controls, and JSZip CDN script.
- `style.css`: Responsive and role-play layout styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/sample.mcpack`: First archive test input.
- `/tmp/opencode/repaired.mcpack`: First repaired archive output; unsafe normalized `outside.txt` remained before the latest fix.
- `/tmp/opencode/sample2.mcaddon`: Test archive for retesting unsafe paths, malformed JSON, and binary preservation.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_server.py`: Local OpenAI-compatible mock server used for prior role-play tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/roleplay_harness.html`: Browser harness used for prior role-play mock tests.

## Important Context
- Project files remain uncommitted and appear as untracked files in `git status`.
- The first archive test confirmed manifest repair and byte-for-byte binary preservation, but showed that calling `archive.remove()` with JSZip’s unsafe original path did not remove the normalized entry. `app.js` now removes unsafe entries by `entry.name`; this fix is not yet browser-tested.
- `/tmp/opencode/sample2.mcaddon` includes valid and malformed JSON, traversal and absolute paths, and binary data.
- Archive repair leaves malformed JSON unchanged.
- The existing server at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` served the app successfully; starting another server on that port failed because it was already in use.

content.text:
It can be made to use a GIF, but that probably wouldn’t help the model. The current flow already turns the video into **five timestamped still images** and sends those to the vision endpoint. That’s a common way to give an image-capable model a sense of motion when the endpoint doesn’t accept video directly.

A GIF would still need to be decoded into frames, and many OpenAI-compatible vision servers treat an animated GIF as just its first frame—or don’t accept GIFs at all. Converting video to GIF can also make a larger, lower-quality file, and it loses audio. The current approach lets the app choose and label the frames it sends.

The tradeoff is that five frames can miss quick or subtle movement. More samples could help, but would increase request size and processing time.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish Blocksmith, a browser app for creating, validating, and repairing Minecraft Bedrock add-ons, with separate role-play and video-analysis features.
- Export the finished app as an Android APK.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and saves chat history and the character/scene prompt in browser storage.
- Do not override model or server safety policies; the 2M-token context target is informational.
- Inspect and safely repair `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archives in-browser while preserving binary assets.
- Video analysis must cover the entire clip as an animated GIF and accept videos up to 1 GB.
- Export the finished app as an APK.

## Decisions
- Archive inspection/repair uses JSZip via CDN, with file-count, expanded-size, and path-safety limits.
- Role-play and video requests use the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint.
- Video conversion uses gif.js, sampling the full clip at 4 fps and scaling to at most 480 px wide; animated-GIF interpretation depends on the selected endpoint.
- APK packaging was started using Capacitor 8; the intended debug APK export is `dist/Blocksmith.apk`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, and persistent role-play view.
- Retested archive repair: unsafe traversal/absolute entries were absent; malformed JSON was unchanged; binary data was preserved exactly.
- Checked role-play layout at tablet and phone widths with long history: no horizontal overflow; history remained scrollable.
- Implemented full-duration GIF conversion, 1 GB input limit, animated-GIF request payload, and failure/status handling.
- Mock-tested full-duration frame sampling, GIF payload, configured model, success state, HTTP 503 feedback, and 1 GB rejection.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Began Capacitor packaging by adding a root `package.json`.

### Active
- Complete Capacitor Android project setup, build a debug APK, export it to `dist/Blocksmith.apk`, and verify the artifact.

### Blocked
- Live model testing requires a configured, reachable vision-capable endpoint that can interpret animated GIFs.

## Next Move
1. Add the web-asset copy and APK export scripts, configure Capacitor, and install its dependencies.
2. Generate/sync the Android project and run the APK build.
3. Verify `dist/Blocksmith.apk` exists and rerun relevant syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, archive validation/repair, role-play, and full-video GIF analysis.
- `index.html`: App UI and JSZip/gif.js CDN includes.
- `style.css`: App and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Initial Capacitor dependencies and Android build/export scripts; packaging is not yet complete.

## Important Context
- GIF.js and its worker load from jsDelivr; the GIF data is sent as a data URL in an OpenAI-compatible multimodal request.
- The 1 GB limit applies to the source video; browser memory and server payload limits may still constrain large clips.
- APK packaging has only just started; no APK has been built or exported yet.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith and export it as an Android APK.
- Publish the APK as a GitHub release titled **Blockbench V1.0 (Dev Build)**.

## Requirements
- GGUF models run on a separate server; role-play uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and saves chat history and character/scene prompts in browser storage.
- Do not override model or server safety policies; the 2M-token context target is informational.
- Safely inspect and repair `.mcaddon`/`.mcpack` archives in-browser while preserving binary assets.
- Analyze the entire video clip as an animated GIF and accept videos up to 1 GB.
- Export the finished app as an APK.

## Decisions
- Archive handling uses JSZip via CDN, with file-count, expanded-size, and path-safety limits.
- Role-play and video requests use the configured OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint.
- Video conversion samples the full clip at 4 fps, scales to at most 480 px wide, and submits an animated GIF; endpoint interpretation depends on model support.
- Capacitor 8 packages the app; the debug APK is `dist/Blocksmith.apk`.
- GitHub release uses tag `v1.0.0-dev` and the title **Blockbench V1.0 (Dev Build)**.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the add-on studio, project library, validator, documentation/research views, server settings, `.mcaddon` generation, persistent role-play view, and full-video GIF analysis.
- Mock-tested full-duration frame sampling, GIF payload, configured model, success and HTTP 503 feedback, and 1 GB rejection.
- Retested archive repair for traversal/absolute entries, malformed JSON, and exact binary preservation.
- Built and verified the APK; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Committed app sources and Android project as `ec3473d` and pushed to `main`.
- Published the prerelease with the APK asset: https://github.com/katie9091/PlayGround/releases/tag/v1.0.0-dev

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- Live model testing requires a configured, reachable vision-capable endpoint that can interpret animated GIFs.

## Next Move
1. If further release work is requested, continue from the published `v1.0.0-dev` prerelease.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Add-on generation, archive validation/repair, role-play, and video analysis.
- `index.html`: App UI and JSZip/gif.js CDN includes.
- `style.css`: App and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Capacitor dependencies and Android build/export scripts.
- `capacitor.config.json`: Capacitor app identity and web directory.
- `android/`: Generated Capacitor Android project.
- `scripts/copy-web-assets.mjs`: Copies web assets for the Android build.
- `scripts/export-apk.mjs`: Exports the built APK to `dist/Blocksmith.apk`.
- `dist/Blocksmith.apk`: Built APK; attached to the GitHub release.

## Important Context
- APK: `dist/Blocksmith.apk` (3.95 MiB); SHA-256 `12b40a9056793f944f402618b4abf6707a77440646c19d66e137e39a4c7c7d8e`.
- The APK is debug-signed and its installed Android app label remains **Blocksmith**; **Blockbench V1.0 (Dev Build)** is the GitHub release title.
- The source commit is `ec3473d595d0d35a7ec1b9a9659f5205d7f462ba` on `main`; the release tag is `v1.0.0-dev`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update Blocksmith’s Create add-on workflow for **V1.0 (Dev Build) Prototype A** so users can upload an existing `.mcaddon`, describe fixes, and update it.
- Earlier APK and GitHub release work is complete.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on**.
- Replace the new-idea prompt with a request for what needs fixing; do not impose a text-length limit.
- Let users update existing add-ons while preserving their existing assets.
- Keep model requests on the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- The existing app uses JSZip for archive inspection and repair, with safety limits.
- The configured model server is required for model-assisted changes to an uploaded add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- APK published to https://github.com/katie9091/PlayGround/releases/tag/v1.0.0-dev; source commit `ec3473d595d0d35a7ec1b9a9659f5205d7f462ba` is on `main`.

### Active
- Prototype A implementation is underway. `index.html`’s Create view intro now says “What needs to be fixed?” and identifies “BLOCKSMITH · PROTOTYPE A”; this edit is uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add `.mcaddon` upload and an unbounded fixes-request field to the Create view.
2. Implement model-assisted archive updates that preserve unchanged binary assets and export the updated add-on.
3. Test the workflow and report any archive/model limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Create view UI; intro copy has been updated for Prototype A.
- `app.js`: Prompt handling, model requests, archive inspection, pack rendering and download.
- `style.css`: Create view styling.

## Important Context
- Current APK: `dist/Blocksmith.apk`; published release title **Blockbench V1.0 (Dev Build)**.
- The released APK predates Prototype A; the current UI edit has not been committed or released.

## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 (Dev Build) Prototype A so users can upload an existing `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export an updated add-on while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and change the prompt to ask what needs fixing, with no text limit.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use the existing JSZip archive support and safety limits.
- Existing add-on updates require the configured model server.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the Create view intro to identify “BLOCKSMITH · PROTOTYPE A” and ask “What needs to be fixed?”
- Added `.mcaddon` upload UI, a fixes prompt with “No character limit” copy, and removed the starter-idea suggestions.
- Added basic upload UI event wiring in `app.js`; full archive-loading functionality is not implemented.

### Active
- Implement safe archive loading and model-assisted text-file updates that preserve binary assets.
- Remove the existing 800-character generation check and complete update/export workflow.
- Test the end-to-end flow.

### Blocked
- `(none)`

## Next Move
1. Implement `loadSafeAddonArchive` and the update/model/merge/export functions in `app.js`.
2. Remove the remaining prompt length restriction and ensure the UI reflects update state.
3. Test archive safety, text updates, binary preservation, and export.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Prototype A intro, add-on upload, fixes prompt, and changed empty-state copy.
- `app.js`: Existing generation and archive validation; upload handler added but calls undefined `loadSafeAddonArchive`; generation still has the old 800-character limit.
- `style.css`: Existing styles; upload-specific styling has not yet been added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. The failed large `app.js` edit made no changes; its replacement did not match the current file.
- The APK/release predates Prototype A; release URL: https://github.com/katie9091/PlayGround/releases/tag/v1.0.0-dev. Source commit on `main`: `ec3473d595d0d35a7ec1b9a9659f5205d7f462ba`.

## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 Prototype A so users can upload an existing `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export the updated add-on while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and ask what needs fixing, with no text limit.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use existing JSZip support and archive safety limits.
- Require the configured model server to update an existing add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the Create view intro, upload UI, fixes prompt, and empty-state copy in `index.html`.
- Added upload/remove UI event wiring and button-state updates in `app.js`.
- Added initial archive-loading and model-update helper functions to `app.js`.

### Active
- Fix and complete the archive helper implementation, including preview and JSZip export that preserve binary assets.
- Replace the generation flow for uploaded add-ons and remove the 800-character prompt check.
- Test archive safety, text updates, binary preservation, and export.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix the newly added helpers in `app.js`; check the duplicate `safeArchivePath` declaration and escaped newline/NUL handling.
2. Update the generate handler, preview, and download flow for uploaded archives; remove the prompt length check.
3. Test archive safety, update handling, binary preservation, and export.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Upload handlers, newly added archive/update helpers, generation, preview, and download logic.
- `index.html`: Create view upload UI and JSZip script inclusion.
- `style.css`: Existing styles; upload-specific styling has not been added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed `M app.js` and `M index.html`.
- The upload handler calls `loadSafeAddonArchive`; the helper has now been added, but needs review and testing.
- `safeArchivePath` already exists later in `app.js`; the new helper defines it again.
- The current generate handler still rejects prompts over 800 characters. `renderPack` and the custom `zip(files)` helper still assume text contents, so uploaded binary assets cannot yet be safely previewed/exported.
- Archive limits: `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=64*1024*1024`, `MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES=128*1024*1024`, `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES=32*1024*1024`, `MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES=1000`.

## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 Prototype A so users can upload an existing `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export the updated add-on while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and allow an unrestricted fixes prompt.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use existing JSZip support and archive safety limits.
- Require the configured model server to update an existing add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated Create view intro, upload UI, fixes prompt, and empty-state copy in `index.html`.
- Added upload/remove UI event wiring and button-state updates in `app.js`.
- Added archive-safety and model-update helper functions in `app.js`.
- Inspected archive/update helpers and identified duplicate path validation and incorrect escaping; no fixes have been made yet.

### Active
- Resolve duplicate `safeArchivePath` declarations and verify NUL/newline handling.
- Wire uploads into generation, preview, and download; remove the 800-character prompt rejection.
- Test archive safety, model updates, binary preservation, and export.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix and consolidate archive path validation; correct NUL and newline handling.
2. Connect uploaded archives to the configured model, safe preview, and JSZip export; remove the prompt-length rejection.
3. Test archive safety, text updates, binary preservation, and export.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Upload wiring, archive/update helpers, generation, preview, validation, and download logic.
- `index.html`: Create view upload UI, unrestricted fixes prompt, and JSZip script inclusion.
- `style.css`: Existing styles; upload-specific styling has not been added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed `M app.js` and `M index.html`.
- `app.js` defines `safeArchivePath` twice, at lines 87 and 117.
- The generate handler still rejects prompts over 800 characters and does not use the upload/update helpers.
- `renderPack` and the custom `zip(files)` helper assume text contents, so uploaded binary assets are not yet safely previewed/exported.
- Archive limits are `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=64*1024*1024`, `MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES=128*1024*1024`, `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES=32*1024*1024`, and `MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES=1000`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 Prototype A so users can upload an existing `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export the updated add-on while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and allow an unrestricted fixes prompt.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use existing JSZip support and archive safety limits.
- Require the configured model server to update an existing add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated Create view intro, upload UI, fixes prompt, and empty-state copy in `index.html`.
- Added upload/remove UI wiring and archive/update helper functions in `app.js`.
- Confirmed JSZip is already loaded in `index.html`.

### Active
- Resolve duplicate `safeArchivePath` declarations and correct NUL/newline handling in `app.js`.
- Wire uploads into generation, preview, and download; remove the 800-character prompt rejection.
- Test archive safety, model updates, binary preservation, and export.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Consolidate archive-path validation; fix NUL checks and newline escaping in update context and model prompt.
2. Connect uploaded archive updates to generation and safe preview/export using JSZip; remove the prompt-length rejection.
3. Test archive safety, text updates, binary preservation, and export.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Upload wiring, archive/update helpers, generation, preview, validation, and download logic.
- `index.html`: Create view upload UI, unrestricted fixes prompt, and JSZip script inclusion.
- `style.css`: Existing styles; upload-specific styling has not been added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed `M app.js` and `M index.html`.
- `app.js` defines `safeArchivePath` twice; the later declaration conflicts with the earlier one’s optional directory handling.
- Update helpers currently use escaped `\\0` and `\\n` sequences, which do not behave as intended for NUL detection and newlines.
- The generate handler still rejects prompts over 800 characters and does not use the upload/update helpers.
- `renderPack` and the custom `zip(files)` helper assume text contents, so uploaded binary assets are not yet safely previewed/exported.
- Archive limits are `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=64*1024*1024`, `MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES=128*1024*1024`, `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES=32*1024*1024`, and `MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES=1000`.

## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 Prototype A so users can upload a `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export changes while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and allow an unrestricted fixes prompt.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use existing JSZip support and archive safety limits.
- Require the configured model server to update an existing add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated Create view copy and UI for upload, fixes prompt, and empty state in `index.html`.
- Added upload/remove UI wiring and archive/update helper functions in `app.js`.
- Confirmed JSZip is already loaded in `index.html`.

### Active
- Consolidate the duplicate `safeArchivePath` declarations and correct NUL/newline handling in `app.js`.
- Wire archive updates into generation, preview, and download; remove the 800-character prompt rejection.
- Test archive safety, model updates, binary preservation, and export.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix and consolidate archive path validation and update-context escaping.
2. Connect uploaded archive updates to generation and make preview/export preserve binary entries through JSZip.
3. Remove the prompt-length rejection and test safety, updates, binary preservation, and export.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Upload handling, archive/update helpers, generation, preview, validation, and download logic.
- `index.html`: Create view upload UI, unrestricted fixes prompt, and JSZip script inclusion.
- `style.css`: Existing styles; upload-specific styling has not been added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed `M app.js` and `M index.html`.
- `app.js` defines `safeArchivePath` at lines 87 and 117; the later declaration overrides the earlier one.
- `getUpdateContext` checks for the literal `\\0` and uses `\\n` sequences, so NUL detection and context formatting are incorrect.
- The generate handler still rejects prompts over 800 characters and does not use the upload/update helpers.
- `renderPack` and the custom `zip(files)` helper assume text contents, so uploaded binary assets are not yet safely previewed or exported.
- Archive limits: 64 MB upload, 128 MB expanded, 32 MB per entry, 1,000 entries.

## Objective
- Complete Blocksmith V1.0 Prototype A so users can upload a `.mcaddon`, describe fixes without a text-length limit, and export changes while preserving existing assets.

## Requirements
- Put `.mcaddon` upload in **Create add-on** and allow an unrestricted fixes prompt.
- Preserve existing assets when updating an uploaded add-on.
- Use the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint for model-assisted changes; do not override model or server safety policies.
- Safely inspect archives and preserve binary assets.

## Decisions
- Use existing JSZip support and archive safety limits.
- Require the configured model server to update an existing add-on.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added upload/remove UI and unrestricted fixes prompt in `index.html`.
- Connected uploaded add-ons to server-based update generation; generated updates are restricted to safe text paths and validated before application.
- Added safe archive loading, update context extraction, binary-aware preview, and JSZip export of the original archive with changes.
- Removed the 800-character prompt rejection and corrected archive path validation consolidation and update-context escaping.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Fix directory-entry handling in validator `inspectArchive`, which still calls `safeArchivePath` without the directory flag.
- Test archive safety, model updates, binary preservation, preview, and export.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Pass `entry.dir` to `safeArchivePath` in `inspectArchive` and verify validator behavior for directory entries.
2. Run archive/update/export tests, including malformed paths, NUL-containing text, binary assets, and long prompts.
3. Review the final diff; changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Archive validation, upload/update flow, preview, and export.
- `index.html`: Create view upload UI, unrestricted fixes prompt, and JSZip inclusion.

## Important Context
- Archive limits: 64 MB upload, 128 MB expanded, 32 MB per entry, 1,000 entries.
- Uploaded add-ons require server mode; demo generation remains available when no add-on is uploaded.
- Current uncommitted changes are in `app.js` and `index.html`.
